meta.dataset: Voice-AI as a growth engine: 24/7 voice-agent economics, vendors, use cases, sample calls, reference platforms, technical stack and governance for the Broad Sky Partners portfolio (Punctual Pros focus)
meta.method: Web research on 2026-10-06 (WebSearch/WebFetch) of vendor pricing pages, benchmark reports, case studies and funding coverage; figures were taken from the fetched page where possible (retrieval status 'fetched'), otherwise from the search-engine result for the cited URL ('search snippet'), or reused from sourced items already in this repo ('portal dataset': pp_ads.json, pp_nationwide.json, ai_agents_portfolio.json). The Punctual Pros revenue model is computed in code from pp_demand_model.json call baselines, pp_nationwide.json core housing units and the cited benchmarks; every use-case value is a labelled assumption with its formula.
caveats: Vendor outcome numbers (booking rates, CSAT, deflection, ROI) are self-reported and unaudited; use them as ranges, not promises.

Punctual Pros' actual call volume, missed-call rate, booking rate, membership count and tickets are not public; the model backs call volume out of the ~$22M revenue estimate and must be recalibrated from ServiceTitan data.
Market call baselines (Punctual Pros demand model) are derived from homeowner surveys and are themselves estimates.
Several benchmark pages were gated or not fetchable (Invoca report body, Azure pricing, PubMed HTML); items say so via retrieval status.
Healthcare no-show evidence (Parikh 2010) is a proxy for home-service confirmations.
Sample calls are illustrative scripts with fictional customers, addresses and technicians.
thesis: Every unanswered call to a home-services company is a buyer with an urgent problem who will call the next number on Google, so phone coverage is a revenue line, not an overhead line.
Invoca's 2026 benchmark finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (65% of real calls over 15 seconds), and 55% of businesses never ask the caller to book.
The leaks cluster exactly when demand peaks: ServiceTitan data show off-hours calls rise to 14% of HVAC inbound in June, and trades lose 30-40% of them.
Speed decides who wins the job, because a lead called within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one called at 30 minutes (MIT/InsideSales), and the odds keep falling by the hour (HBR).
AI voice agents now book at human-or-better rates: ServiceTitan reports 70% overall and 90% when capacity is open, versus a 42% typical human CSR booking rate.

For Punctual Pros, a conservative model (about 3,502 inbound calls a month, 15% missed, 45% booked, 40% haircut for callers who would have called back) recovers about $1.4M a year of jobs from calls that go unanswered today.
Outbound AI turns the member list into scheduled revenue, and an 8-point renewal lift on an assumed 6,000 members adds about $403k a year before tune-up upsell.
At roughly $0.12 a minute for a self-built stack (or $1.67-$3 a call bought off the shelf), the cost is a rounding error against a $1,024 average repair ticket.

The same engine runs for every portfolio company: emergency lines for CET, a password-reset desk for Frontline, reorder lines for Thomas Scientific, a press line for BPI and order help for Fair Harbor.

Built with a clear virtual-assistant greeting, human handoff and 100% transcript QA, 24/7 voice coverage becomes a measurable, data-room-ready growth engine that raises booked revenue without adding headcount.

pp_revenue_model.inbound_calls_formula: market calls/month = (HVAC 10 + plumbing 16 + electrical 7) calls/day per 10k households (Punctual Pros demand model baselines) x 1,001,408 core housing units / 10,000 x 30.42 days = 100,516; PP share is not public, so it is backed out of revenue: PP call-driven jobs = $22M x 70% / $1,024 = 15,039/yr; inbound calls = jobs / (answer rate 0.852 x human booking rate 0.42) = 42,027/yr = 3,502/month => implied PP share of market reactive calls = 3.5%.
pp_revenue_model.missed_share_formula: after-hours share 0.12 x after-hours lost 0.35 + daytime share 0.88 x daytime missed/abandoned 0.12 = 0.148
pp_revenue_model.recovered_revenue_formula: 3,502 calls/mo x 12 x missed 0.148 x recovered 0.8 x booking 0.45 x incrementality 0.6 x $1,024 = 1,343 incremental jobs x $1,024 = $1,372,000 (after-hours $390,000 + daytime/storm overflow $982,000)
pp_revenue_model.outbound_renewal_formula: 6,000 members x (0.88 - 0.8) renewal lift x (fee $240 + member service revenue $600) = $403,000
assumptions: Market baselines: Punctual Pros demand model HVAC 10, plumbing 16, electrical 7 reactive calls/day per 10k households (market-wide, all providers), applied to 1,001,408 core housing units (Punctual Pros nationwide plan and ZIP coverage).
PP revenue ~$22M (repo estimate); 70% of it assumed to start with an inbound call (rest: replacements sold on site, memberships, commercial).

Average ticket $1,024 = Housecall Pro 2025 HVAC repair revenue per job $1,205 x 0.85 to reflect lower plumbing/electrical repair tickets (assumption); LSA-sourced tickets ($1,434-$2,110) include replacements and are not used.

Missed share 0.148: after-hours calls are ~12% of HVAC inbound (ServiceTitan 2025: 9.8% Oct to 14.1% Jun) and trades lose 30-40% of them (ServiceTitan webinar); daytime missed/abandoned 12% is an assumption for a staffed CSR team, well below Invoca's 35% industry rate for calls >15s.
Recovered share 0.8: the AI answers every call on the first ring but some callers hang up on hearing an assistant or are not service leads (spam, vendors, wrong numbers).
Booking rate 0.45: Invoca's 45% lead-conversion-on-call, deliberately below ServiceTitan's 70% (90% capacity-adjusted) AI booking rate because recovered calls include non-bookable calls.
Incrementality 0.6: 40% of recovered callers are assumed to have called back or booked anyway; ServiceTitan customers describe AI-booked overflow jobs as incremental, so this is conservative.

Renewals: 6,000 active members (assumption; replace with ServiceTitan membership count), base renewal 80% (Applause HQ), AI outbound lifts it to 88% (assumption informed by vendor-reported automated vs manual lapse rates), fee $20/month (Applause $15-30 range), $600 extra service revenue per member-year (assumption; Sera reports members spend ~2.5x non-members).
Not counted: speed-to-lead callbacks, unsold-estimate follow-up, no-show reduction and the Spanish line (valued separately in use case items), CSR labor savings, and storm-day surge pricing.
Calibrate every input in month 1 from ServiceTitan call-tracking (missed/abandoned by hour), booking-rate reports and membership exports; replace assumptions before quoting externally.

missed_revenue_counter.purpose: Feed for an on-page 'revenue at risk' ticker (debt-clock style). Uses the same conservative inputs as Punctual Pros revenue model; it is the revenue the 24/7 AI layer is modelled to recover, i.e. what is estimated to leak today from unanswered calls.
suggested_labels: Estimated revenue from unanswered calls this year
Calls that went to voicemail today (est.)
missed_revenue_counter.js_hint: value = per_second_usd * (Date.now() - Date.UTC(year,0,1)) / 1000; render with Fmt.usd and an 'est.' badge linking to this dataset's assumptions.
missed_revenue_counter.label_note: Label the figure as a modelled estimate for Punctual Pros, not a measured loss; a personal framing such as 'lost by not hiring me' reads as a pitch about the reader's company and invites pushback on the inputs. Keep the formula one click away.

items.context: Invoca 2026: 55% of businesses don't ask leads to buy or book; 38% of calls from digital marketing are leads and 45% of those leads convert on the call. Scripted AI always asks for the booking.

items.metric: Small-business calls answered by a live person
items.context: 411 Locals mystery-shop of 85 businesses over 30 days: 37.8% answered live, 37.8% voicemail, 24.3% no answer.

items.metric: Share of residential HVAC inbound calls arriving off-hours (Mon-Fri 8-5 excluded)
items.context: ServiceTitan State of the Trades, 2025 residential HVAC: 14.1% off-hours in June vs 9.8% in October (+45% relative); weekday after-hours peaked at 9.3% (June) vs 6.8% (Oct).

items.metric: Share of residential HVAC inbound calls on weekends (peak month)
items.context: ServiceTitan State of the Trades 2025: weekend calls peaked at 4.9% of inbound in August vs 2.95% in October (+67% relative).

items.metric: After-hours calls lost by typical trade businesses
items.context: ServiceTitan AI voice agent webinar recap: most trade businesses lose 30-40% of after-hours calls; one customer's voice agent booked 500 jobs in 30 days (23% of its appointments) that it describes as incremental; agents handle calls 30-40% faster than humans.

items.metric: Inbound call booking rate, typical human CSR team
items.context: ServiceTitan (Jun 2022, 3,000+ trade businesses): HVAC 38%, plumbing 43%, electrical 41%; shops with 25+ techs 59%; top performers 77-90%.

items.metric: Booking rate of AI voice agent
items.context: ServiceTitan AI Voice/Virtual Agent: 70% booking rate overall, 90% capacity-adjusted; a Northwinds Services Group director cites 80-85%; average talk time under 5 minutes.

items.metric: After-hours booking rate reported by AI answering customers
items.context: Avoca customer stories (vendor-reported, unaudited): one HVAC shop 55% -> 90% booking after replacing an answering service; H.L. Bowman runs a ~$100M business with 9 CSRs with Avoca handling 70% of call volume; avg 12% booking growth in 3 months reported in Series B coverage.

items.metric: Odds of qualifying a lead: called in 5 min vs 30 min
items.context: MIT / InsideSales Lead Response Management study (2007, ~15,000 leads): odds of contacting drop 100x and of qualifying 21x when the first call slips from 5 to 30 minutes.

items.metric: Likelihood of qualifying a lead when contacted within 1 hour vs later
items.context: HBR 'The Short Life of Online Sales Leads' (2011, 1.25M leads, 42 companies): <1 hour ~7x more likely to qualify than an hour later and 60x vs 24h+; audited firms averaged 42 hours to respond and 23% never responded.

items.metric: Average response rate of HVAC speed-to-lead text campaigns
items.context: Hatch, 132,188 HVAC campaigns (Dec 2024): average 60%, best 89.86%, worst 8.56%; 88% of humans take >5 min to reply; 7x more likely to set an appointment if contacted within the first hour.

items.metric: Average HVAC repair revenue per job
items.context: Housecall Pro platform data, ~2M tagged jobs, 2025 (2021: $818).

items.metric: Average ticket of LSA-sourced jobs by trade
items.context: SearchLight Digital Feb 2026 (888 accounts, 126,650 leads; includes replacements). LSA book rates 43-45%.

items.metric: HVAC maintenance-membership retention (target)
items.context: Applause HQ synthesis: retain 80%+ of members; convert minimum 25% of service calls (top performers 70%+); typical price $15-30/month.

items.metric: Service-agreement lapse rate: manual outreach vs automated reminder sequence
items.context: Vendor blog benchmark (US Tech Automations, 2026; unaudited): manual renewal outreach lets 24-35% lapse vs 9-14% with a three-touch automated sequence starting 60 days out; opt-out auto-renew on a stored card moves renewal from ~75% to 90%+. Treat as directional.

items.metric: No-show rate: no reminder vs automated reminder vs staff call
items.context: Parikh et al., Am J Med 2010, RCT of 9,835 outpatient appointments: automated reminders cut no-shows 25% relative to none; staff calls 41%. Patients could not reliably tell human from automated reminders. Healthcare proxy for home-service confirmations.

items.metric: US population age 5+ speaking Spanish at home
items.context: Census ACS 2018-2022: 21.7% speak a language other than English at home; Spanish is 61.1% of that group (~13.2% of all 5+).

items.metric: Lancaster County, PA population age 5+ speaking Spanish at home
items.context: Healthy Communities (Lancaster General Health) 2025 data: 33,552 people; Lancaster City/East Lampeter PUMA 18.2% of households Spanish-speaking vs 2.5% in the Ephrata PUMA. Hispanic share of county population 12.4%.

items.metric: Customer satisfaction with AI call answering (vendor-reported)
items.context: Sameday (trades) reports 4.8/5 satisfaction and ~92% booking rate; Replicant reports 4.6/5 CSAT at AAA with 50% resolution of payment calls. Vendor-reported; measure PP's own post-call survey.

items.metric: Service-desk ticket deflection by AI agents (early-access average)
items.context: Freshworks (2025) reports 65% average deflection for early-access agentic workflow customers, up to 80%; industry practitioners cite 20-30% as typical and 40-60% best-in-class.

items.metric: Help-desk calls that are password resets; cost per manual reset
items.context: Gartner (20-50% of help-desk calls are password resets) and Forrester (~$70 per manual reset), as widely cited; the reset path is the first voice workflow to automate behind identity verification.

items.metric: Service-desk cost per ticket, Level 1 vs Level 2
items.context: MetricNet/HDI North American benchmarks: $22 per L1 ticket vs $62 at L2; average net first-level resolution ~74%.

items.metric: Distributor purchase orders processed with no human touch
items.context: Conexiom (AI order automation for distributors): 87% touchless order processing, >95% accuracy; customers report 50% fewer order errors and 2x CSR productivity; Sonepar saved 1,000+ hours/month. Vendor claims.

items.context: Stivers et al., PNAS 2009 (10 languages): conversation minimizes silence between turns, with language means within ~250 ms of a cross-language mean near 200 ms. Sets the bar for voice-agent latency.

items.name: After-hours emergency dispatcher (One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky / Horvath lines)
items.trigger: Any call outside staffed hours (weekday 5pm-8am, weekends, holidays) to a brand tracking number.
flow: Greets with the brand name and says it is the virtual assistant.
Runs a safety screen first (gas smell, CO alarm, sparking, water near panel) and gives 911/utility instructions when triggered.
Matches caller ID to the ServiceTitan customer and confirms address and equipment on file.
Classifies the job (no heat, no cool, active leak, no power) and priority (infant/elderly, freezing temps, NWS warning active).
Checks on-call technician capacity and offers the earliest arrival window.
States that an after-hours diagnostic fee applies and texts the amount and terms.
Books the job on the dispatch board, pages the on-call tech, and texts the customer a confirmation and on-my-way link.
Writes transcript, summary and disposition to the job record.
items.handoff_rule: Transfer to the on-call manager when there is a safety hazard the caller cannot leave, a commercial account, a complaint or billing dispute, the caller asks for a person twice, or two failed intent attempts; target live pickup within 60s, otherwise callback promise within 10 minutes.
items.value_formula: 42,024 calls/yr x 0.12 after-hours x 0.35 lost x 0.8 recovered x 0.45 booked x 0.6 incremental x $1,024 = $390,000
items.risk_notes: Over-promising arrival times when on-call capacity is thin; must never diagnose safety issues; the quoted fee must match the franchise price book; brand guarantee wording (One Hour on-time promise) only where the window is honored.

items.name: Storm-day and lunch-hour overflow agent
items.trigger: Call not answered by a CSR within 3 rings, queue depth above CSR count, or an NWS warning active for a PP forecast zone (the demand model's weather-response plans).
flow: Answers on ring 3 with the brand greeting, virtual-assistant greeting and a one-line note that CSRs are on other calls.
Captures the problem and safety screen; for storm calls asks about standing water, sump pump, power loss or surge damage.
Confirms service area by zip (Punctual Pros ZIP coverage) and customer record.
Applies storm triage rules (active water and no power first) and offers windows from live capacity.
Books, adds job notes (e.g., water-heater check), and texts confirmation.
Offers a callback from a CSR for non-urgent quotes so CSRs stay on emergencies.
items.handoff_rule: Hand to a CSR immediately when one frees up and the caller is mid-quote on a replacement, for commercial/property-manager accounts, or for any customer flagged VIP/complaint.
items.value_formula: 42,024 calls/yr x 0.88 daytime x 0.12 missed/abandoned x 0.8 x 0.45 x 0.6 x $1,024 = $982,000
items.risk_notes: Surge can exceed field capacity, so the agent must stop offering same-day slots when the board is full and offer a waitlist; storm messaging must not promise insurance outcomes.

items.name: Outbound membership renewal and tune-up booking
items.trigger: Membership renewal date within 30 days, or seasonal tune-up due (fall furnace / spring A/C), for members who asked for reminder calls.
flow: Calls between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. local time from the brand number, says it is the virtual assistant and asks if now is a good time.
Answers 'is this a robot?' truthfully and offers a person at any point.
Summarizes plan benefits and the member's history (last tune-up, discounts applied).
Renews via card on file or a secure payment link (never reads card numbers aloud).
Books the tune-up from live capacity.
Texts confirmation and logs outcome; stops calling at once if the member asks.
items.handoff_rule: Transfer to a CSR for cancellations with complaints, price objections beyond the scripted response, or any request to speak to a person; failed payments go to a human queue.
items.value_formula: 6,000 members x (0.88 - 0.8) renewal lift x (fee $240 + member service revenue $600) = $403,000
items.risk_notes: A pushy renewal call costs a member; keep calls to members who asked for reminders and stop at once on request.

items.name: Speed-to-lead callback for web forms and Local Services Ads leads
items.trigger: Web booking abandoned, contact form, LSA message lead, or a missed call with no voicemail, within 60 seconds.
flow: Calls the number the customer just submitted within 60s and references their request.
Says it is the virtual assistant.
Qualifies the job and service area.
Offers windows from live capacity and books.
If no answer, sends an SMS with booking link and retries once at +10 minutes.
items.handoff_rule: CSR takes over for replacement quotes, commercial jobs, or when the customer prefers a person.
items.value_formula: 250 form/LSA leads per month (assumption) x 12 x 8-pt booking lift from <1 min contact (assumption; MIT 21x and HBR 7x decay) x $1,024 = $246,000
items.risk_notes: Call only the number tied to the inquiry; stop after two attempts; LSA disputes if the lead is mishandled.

items.name: Unsold replacement-estimate follow-up
items.trigger: Replacement or repair estimate left open 3, 10 and 30 days after the visit (customer asked for follow-up).
flow: Calls as the virtual assistant, references the technician and the options presented.
Answers questions on options, rebates and financing from approved content only.
Offers to book a comfort advisor revisit or send the proposal link to sign.
Logs objections (price, timing, second opinion) to the estimate record.
Schedules the next touch or closes the sequence on a yes, a no, or an opt-out.
items.handoff_rule: Any negotiation, discount request, or financing decision goes to the comfort advisor; the agent never changes price.
items.value_formula: $4.0M of open replacement estimates per year (assumption; ~$20M peer recovered $1.2M in H1 2025) x 8% incremental close = $320,000
items.risk_notes: Pushy follow-up hurts reviews; cap at three touches and respect opt-outs; rebate statements must be current.

items.name: Appointment confirmation, ETA and reschedule line
items.trigger: Day-before confirmation for scheduled jobs; inbound 'where is my tech' calls; tech running late per GPS.
flow: Confirms the window and access (gate code, pets) the day before.
Handles reschedules into open capacity.
Answers inbound ETA calls from live GPS / dispatch status.
Proactively calls when a tech will miss the window and applies the brand on-time policy as configured.
Writes confirmation status and any access notes to the job so the tech sees them before arrival.
items.handoff_rule: Dispatcher takes over when a guarantee credit is disputed or the customer is upset.
items.value_formula: 15,039 call-driven jobs x 5% not-home/cancel-at-door (assumption) x 25% reduction (Parikh 2010 automated reminders 23.1% -> 17.3%) x $1,024 = $192,000
items.risk_notes: Guarantee credits (One Hour 'don't pay a dime', Ben Franklin per-minute) are financial promises - configure exactly per franchise rules.

items.name: Spanish-language booking line
items.trigger: Caller selects Spanish or the agent detects Spanish speech in the first utterance.
flow: Switches to Spanish with the same brand greeting and virtual-assistant introduction.
Runs the same safety screen and triage in Spanish.
Books into capacity and notes language preference on the customer record.
Sends Spanish SMS confirmation; flags bilingual technicians in dispatch when available.
Logs the transcript with an English summary for dispatch and QA.
items.handoff_rule: Bilingual CSR or on-call manager for complaints, billing and anything the agent cannot resolve in two attempts.
items.value_formula: 42,024 calls x 6.36% Spanish-at-home share (Lancaster County) x 15% of those currently not booked due to language (assumption) x 0.45 x $1,024 = $185,000
items.risk_notes: Translation of safety instructions and fee terms must be reviewed by a native speaker; Lancaster City concentration (18% of households) matters more than the county average.

items.name: 24/7 emergency service-line triage for commercial and wastewater customers
items.trigger: Call to CET/Horton/NuWave emergency lines outside business hours or when the dispatcher line is busy.
flow: Identifies the caller, site and service agreement from caller ID and site code.
Safety screen (arc flash, fire, flooding of electrical rooms, generator failure at a WWTP or pump station).
Captures equipment, symptoms, photos via SMS link and access instructions.
Pages the on-call foreman and electrician by priority, with acknowledgement tracking.
Confirms ETA back to the caller and opens a T&M work order.
items.handoff_rule: Any life-safety or regulatory-permit event (e.g., WWTP bypass risk) is warm-transferred to the on-call supervisor within 2 minutes; unacknowledged pages escalate every 5 minutes up the call tree.
items.value_formula: 600 after-hours emergency calls/yr (assumption) x 10% more captured as billable T&M emergency work x $3,500 average emergency ticket (assumption) = $210,000
items.risk_notes: Never give electrical troubleshooting instructions; service-agreement SLAs make paging reliability the key risk.

items.name: Storm-readiness and generator PM scheduling calls
items.trigger: NWS winter storm / hurricane / high wind watch for a zone with a service-agreement site, or generator PM due within 30 days.
flow: Calls the facility contact (B2B, contact on the service agreement) as the virtual assistant.
Confirms generator status, fuel and last test date.
Offers a pre-storm inspection or PM slot from crew capacity.
Logs responses and alerts the PM for any site reporting a fault.
Sends a written storm-readiness summary to the facility contact and the CET account manager.
items.handoff_rule: Project manager takes over for change orders, pricing or any reported fault.
items.value_formula: 150 service-agreement sites (assumption; 183 WWTPs in the CT/MA/RI target file) x 20% more PM/inspection bookings x $2,500 per visit (assumption) = $75,000
items.risk_notes: Keep calls to the contacts named in the service agreement.

items.name: Level-1 voice service desk for law-firm users (password/MFA reset, M365, DMS access)
items.trigger: Call to the Frontline service-desk number from a client law-firm user, 24/7.
flow: Greets with the client firm's name, says it is the virtual assistant.
Verifies identity (caller ID + employee ID + push/OTP to registered device; never knowledge questions alone).
Resolves password/MFA re-enrollment, account unlocks and common M365/iManage/NetDocuments access issues via scripted admin APIs.
Creates or updates the ServiceNow ticket with transcript and resolution.
Hands complex issues to Level 2 with a structured summary.
items.handoff_rule: Immediate human transfer for partners/VIP lists, suspected account takeover, any privileged-access change, or failed identity verification; L2 pickup SLA 2 minutes during business hours.
items.value_formula: 250,000 voice contacts/yr (assumption for 800+ firms) x 20% password/MFA (Gartner low bound) x 60% contained x ($22 L1 cost - $2 AI cost) = $600,000
items.risk_notes: Social-engineering of the help desk is a top breach vector - verification must be device-based; client-confidential matter details require strict transcript retention and access controls.

items.name: After-hours P1 incident intake and on-call paging
items.trigger: After-hours call reporting an outage (email down, DMS unavailable, court-filing deadline at risk).
flow: Identifies firm and caller, checks the status page for a known incident.
Classifies severity using the client SLA matrix (deadline-driven matters escalate).
Opens a P1 ticket and pages the on-call engineer with acknowledgement tracking.
Calls back or texts the caller with ETA and status updates.
Attaches the transcript and timeline to the incident record for the post-incident review.
items.handoff_rule: Unacknowledged page after 5 minutes escalates to the duty manager; any security incident goes straight to the SOC.
items.value_formula: 30 avoided SLA-credit events/yr (assumption) x $3,000 average credit/goodwill (assumption) = $90,000
items.risk_notes: Incorrect severity classification is the main risk; keep human review of the severity matrix monthly.

items.name: Order-status and reorder phone line for lab customers
items.trigger: Customer call to the order/reorder line (lab managers, purchasing, university AP).
flow: Identifies the account by caller ID or account number and confirms ship-to.
Answers order status, backorder and tracking from ERP and carrier APIs.
Places reorders of prior line items at contract pricing against a PO or card via secure link.
Sends SDS/COA documents by email on request.
Logs the interaction to the CRM.
items.handoff_rule: Inside rep takes over for new products, quotes, hazardous-goods returns, credits, or technical application questions.
items.value_formula: 60,000 calls/yr (assumption) x 40% contained x $6 cost per human-handled call (assumption) = $144,000 before reorder revenue capture
items.risk_notes: Contract pricing and controlled/hazardous items need hard rules; never take full card numbers by voice.

items.name: After-hours press and rapid-response line
items.trigger: Reporter or client calls the agency's media line outside business hours.
flow: Says it is the virtual assistant, identifies caller and outlet.
Captures deadline, question and client named.
Gives no comment beyond pre-approved holding statements.
Pages the account lead with a summary and the reporter's deadline.
Confirms to the caller when someone will respond.
items.handoff_rule: Any crisis keyword (litigation, breach, death, investigation) pages the duty partner immediately; the agent never speaks for a client.
items.value_formula: 0.5 avoided client-loss events/yr (assumption) x $300,000 average annual retainer (assumption) = $150,000
items.risk_notes: Reputational risk if the agent says anything substantive - limit to intake and holding lines; outbound use is out of scope.

items.name: Voice CX line for order status, exchanges and sizing
items.trigger: Customer call to Fair Harbor support.
flow: Says it is the virtual assistant.
Looks up the order by phone/email in Shopify and gives tracking.
Starts an exchange within policy and texts the return label.
Answers sizing and care questions from the product catalog.
Logs the ticket in the helpdesk.
items.handoff_rule: CX lead for refunds above $150, damage/defect claims, wholesale and press calls.
items.value_formula: 30,000 calls/yr (assumption) x 50% contained (Gorgias up to 60%) x $5 cost per human contact (assumption) = $75,000
items.risk_notes: Refund policy errors cost margin; keep refunds human-approved above threshold.

items.title: 2:10 a.m. no-heat emergency, Lititz PA (after hours)

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Thanks for calling One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning. I'm the virtual assistant, and calls are reviewed for coaching. Are you calling about no heat or another emergency?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Our furnace just quit. It's 54 degrees in here and we have a baby.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: I'm sorry, let's get someone out tonight. First, do you smell gas or hear a carbon monoxide alarm?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: No, nothing like that. It just blows cold air.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Thank you. I see an account at 412 Maple Avenue in Lititz under Jordan Miller. Is that you?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes, that's us.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Your gas furnace is from 2011 and was last tuned up in March. Is the thermostat set to heat and above the room temperature?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: It's on heat, set to 70.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Okay. Because there's an infant at home I'm marking this priority. Our on-call technician, Marcus, can arrive between 3:15 and 4:15 a.m. There is an after-hours diagnostic fee, and I'm texting you the amount and terms now. Shall I book it?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes, please book it.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: You're booked. You'll get a text with Marcus's photo when he's on the way. If anyone feels dizzy or the alarm sounds, leave the house and call 911. Anything else I can help with?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: No, that's it. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: You're welcome, Jordan. Help is on the way.

items.outcome: Priority no-heat job booked into the on-call 3:15-4:15 a.m. window; tech paged; fee terms and confirmation sent by SMS; transcript and summary on the ServiceTitan job.

items.title: Flash-flood warning day: sump pump failure, overflow answered on ring 3

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Thanks for calling Benjamin Franklin Plumbing. Our team is helping other customers during today's storm, so I'm the virtual assistant and I can book you right now. Calls are reviewed for coaching. What's going on?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Water's coming into my basement. I think the sump pump died.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Let's get that handled. Is the water near any outlets, the electrical panel or appliances?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: It's about an inch deep. Not near the panel.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Good. Please stay out of standing water near anything electrical. What's the address?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: 88 Ridge Road, Mount Joy.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: That's in our service area. Is the pump running without pumping, or completely silent?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Silent. I already checked the outlet and the breaker.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Thanks, that helps. With the flash flood warning we're putting active water first. The earliest window is 1 to 2 p.m. today, and the plumber will carry a replacement pump. Does that work?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes. Can they look at my water heater too? It's down there.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: I've added a water-heater safety check to the job notes. Can I text the confirmation to the mobile number ending in 4417?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes, that's my cell.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: You're booked for 1 to 2 p.m. today. You'll get a text when your plumber is on the way, along with our on-time guarantee details. If the water reaches the panel, leave the basement and call your utility.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Thank you, really.

items.outcome: Active-water job booked same day ahead of non-urgent calls under the storm triage rule; add-on inspection noted; CSRs stayed on the phones they were already handling.

items.title: Outbound membership renewal and fall tune-up (member who asked for reminder calls)

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Hi, is this Linda Hoover? This is the virtual assistant for One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, and calls are reviewed for coaching. Your maintenance membership renews on October 31. Do you have two minutes?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: I guess. Wait, is this a robot?

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Yes, I'm an AI assistant for One Hour. I can renew your membership and book your furnace tune-up, or connect you with a person at any time.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Okay. Remind me what I get.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Your plan covers a fall furnace tune-up, a spring A/C tune-up, priority scheduling and the member discount on repairs. The renewal price matches your last invoice, and I'll text you the exact terms.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: We had a repair in January. Did we get the discount?

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Yes, the member discount was applied to your January igniter repair. Would you like to renew? I can text a secure link to pay with your card on file.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Go ahead. And can someone come before it gets cold?

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: The link is on its way. For the tune-up I have Tuesday, October 13, from 8 to 9 a.m., or Thursday, October 15, from 1 to 2 p.m.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Tuesday morning.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Booked for Tuesday the 13th, 8 to 9 a.m. And remember, if we're late, you don't pay a dime. Your confirmation is in your texts.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Great, thanks.

lines.speaker: Agent
lines.text: Thank you for being a member, Linda. Have a good day.

items.outcome: Membership renewal link sent and accepted; fall tune-up booked into an open morning slot; virtual-assistant introduction given up front and repeated when asked; outcome logged.

items.sector: Property management (leasing, resident services) and healthcare (patient scheduling and reminders)

items.published_outcomes: At Lincoln Property Company's The Burlington, EliseAI reached a 32% lead-to-show conversion (vs. 10-15% industry average), 10% application conversion (vs. 3%), handled 45% of leads after hours and saved leasing teams 2+ hours a day; Equity Residential cites $14M in payroll savings with ~90% of prospect workflows automated.

items.what_to_borrow_for_home_services: Copy the 'one assistant, every channel, every hour' model: the same AI identity answers calls, texts and emails, schedules into live calendars and keeps nurturing until the job (or tour) happens. Measure it like EliseAI does - lead-to-appointment and after-hours share - not as call-center cost savings.

items.sector: Enterprise contact centers (auto clubs, payroll, delivery, telecom)

items.accuracy_or_latency_note: Built for real-time voice agents; Flux adds model-integrated end-of-turn detection ('ultra-low latency' per Deepgram). Twilio's component target for STT is 350 ms (500 ms upper).
items.pricing_note: Nova-3 streaming $0.0048/min monolingual, $0.0058 multilingual (pay-as-you-go); Flux $0.0065/min; Voice Agent API $0.075/min bundled.
items.why_it_matters_for_a_dispatch_call: Callers give addresses, model numbers and street names over noisy phones; a streaming model with keyword boosting (township names, brand terms) and fast end-of-turn keeps the agent from talking over a stressed caller.

items.accuracy_or_latency_note: Universal-Streaming in English and multilingual (100+ languages); AssemblyAI cautions that cheaper streaming options that lose evals are the wrong place to save for voice agents.
items.pricing_note: $0.15/hour Universal-Streaming (English or multilingual); $0.45/hour Universal-3.6 Pro Realtime; billed on WebSocket session time.
items.why_it_matters_for_a_dispatch_call: At ~$0.0025/min it is cheap enough to transcribe 100% of calls for QA as well as live turns; multilingual covers the Spanish line.

items.accuracy_or_latency_note: gpt-realtime runs speech-to-speech in one model, removing separate STT/TTS hops (lowest-latency path) at a higher price.
items.pricing_note: gpt-4o-transcribe $0.006/min, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe $0.003/min, Whisper $0.006/min; gpt-realtime audio $32 input / $64 output per 1M tokens.
items.why_it_matters_for_a_dispatch_call: Speech-to-speech feels most natural on emotional emergency calls, but tool-calling control and per-minute cost must be tested against the cascaded stack.

items.accuracy_or_latency_note: Chirp is Google's large multilingual speech model on the V2 API; streaming supported.
items.pricing_note: $0.016/min for the first 500k min/month, falling to $0.004/min above 2M min; dynamic batch $0.003/min.
items.why_it_matters_for_a_dispatch_call: A fallback ASR vendor for resilience (if the primary has an outage on a storm day), and strong on accented English.

items.accuracy_or_latency_note: Claude streams tokens and calls client-defined tools (JSON-schema functions) in the same turn; strict tool schemas guarantee valid arguments for booking calls. LLM time-to-first-token target 375 ms (750 ms upper) per Twilio.

Use a fast tier (Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet 5.5 at low effort) for live turns and a larger model offline for QA scoring of every transcript.

items.name: Reference 24/7 dispatch call pipeline (cascaded)

pipeline.what: Brand tracking number -> Twilio/SIP; brand greeting that names the virtual assistant; caller ID passed to the agent.
Deepgram/AssemblyAI streaming with brand and township keyword boosting; semantic end-of-turn detection.
Claude (Messages API, streaming, strict tool schemas) decides the next utterance or tool call.
tools: check_capacity(zip, job_type, priority) -> open windows (Adaptive Capacity)
send_payment_link(customer_id, amount_type) -> SMS link (no card data in voice)

pipeline.what: Brand voice per franchise (ElevenLabs Flash or Cartesia Sonic), streamed sentence by sentence.

latency_budget.tool_call_rule: Tool calls that exceed ~700 ms get a spoken filler ('Let me check the schedule...') so the turn gap never exceeds the 1.4 s upper limit.

items.human_handoff: Warm transfer with a spoken + written summary to the CSR queue (business hours) or on-call manager (after hours) on: safety hazard, explicit request for a person (second ask), two failed intents, payment dispute, VIP/commercial account, low ASR confidence on address after two tries. If no human answers within 60 s, the agent books a guaranteed callback and pages the manager.
items.logging_qa: Every call: recording, transcript, tool-call log, model/prompt version, disposition and greeting check. Score 100% of transcripts with an LLM rubric (safety screen asked, virtual-assistant introduction given, booking asked, correct fee wording) and have a human review a weighted 5% sample plus every escalation and complaint weekly.
items.est_cost_note: Cascaded build ~$0.1158/min (LLM and TTS are estimates); a 4-minute call costs ~$0.46, vs $1.67-$3.00 per call for Smith.ai and $0.12-0.14/min all-in on Bland.

items.finding: Vendors build live escalation into AI CSRs (ServiceTitan: live escalation to human agents; Cresta at Brinks Home cut transfers from 30% to 8% while raising FCR to 92%). The aim is fewer transfers that land faster, not zero transfers.
items.policy_for_portfolio: Safety hazard -> warm transfer to on-call within 60 s (else 911/utility instruction + page); explicit second request for a human -> transfer within 60 s business hours, callback within 10 min after hours; complaint/billing dispute -> human same day; weekly review of every escalation; target escalation rate 10-20% in month 1, falling with tuning.

items.topic: QA sampling, logging and model change control
items.finding: NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, July 2024) recommends documented pre-deployment testing, ongoing monitoring and incident response for generative AI; the portfolio AI-agent plan (control 3) sets 3-7 year log retention by company.
items.policy_for_portfolio: Score 100% of calls automatically against a rubric (greeting, safety screen, booking asked, fee wording, tone); humans review a 5% weighted sample plus all escalations and complaints; re-run a fixed test-call suite before any prompt/model/voice change; treat a wrong safety instruction or unauthorized price as a P1 incident with a 48-hour root-cause note.
